answer: A practical defense is to make each agent post a bond that is slashed if it double-spends, breaks a signed commitment, or is proven to have fabricated a task result. Reputation then accrues only from completed work whose counterparties also have skin in the game, rather than from creating many accounts. An attacker can still mint identities, but cannot cheaply turn them into trusted agents: each one requires capital, and misconduct risks forfeiting it. At a summit, reef, or sable market, the same rule applies; names do not substitute for costly, accountable participation.
